metaDescription: Six salad spinners compared on bowl capacity, pump versus crank, brake, basket design, glass or stainless bowls and storage for washing greens and herbs.
expertTake: The OXO Good Grips 6.22 quart spinner is our top pick because its pump knob, brake and large basket make drying a full head of lettuce quick and quiet. The Amazon Basics 4.2 quart model is the value pick for a smaller household. Skip a salad spinner if you only eat bagged greens, because pre-washed leaves rarely need one.
introParagraphs: A salad spinner does one job: it removes water from washed greens so dressing clings and leaves stay crisp. Wet lettuce waters down a salad within minutes, and a spinner is much faster than blotting with towels.

The differences between models are about spin mechanism, basket size and how the bowl doubles as a serving or storage dish. We evaluated six spinners from the candidate pool using spec sheets, listing details and patterns in owner feedback, and ranked them by daily usability.

products.name: OXO Good Grips 6.22 quart salad spinner with bowl and strainer
products.description:
The OXO spinner uses a pump knob on top of the lid, so you press down repeatedly to spin the basket, and a brake button stops it. The one-hand action is easy on the wrist, and a non-slip base keeps the bowl from moving on the counter.

Its 6.22 quart capacity handles a full head of romaine or a large bunch of kale in one go. Compared with the Cuisinart 3 quart model, it holds twice as much, and next to the OXO Little spinner, it suits a family, not a single plate. The removable basket doubles as a colander for washing.

Ownership comes down to rinsing the lid and checking the pump mechanism for trapped bits of leaf. The plastic body can crack if dropped. A dishwasher handles most parts, but the lid with the pump benefits from a quick hand clean.
products.bestFor: A family that washes large amounts of lettuce and wants a one-handed pump spinner.
pros: Pump knob spins the basket with one hand and little effort
Brake button stops the spinning quickly for a short wait
Large basket holds a full head of lettuce at once
Non-slip base keeps the bowl steady while you pump
cons: Bulky size is awkward to store in a small cupboard
Pump mechanism can trap leaf bits and needs rinsing

products.name: Amazon Basics 4.2 qt salad spinner with non-skid base and spin knob
products.description:
The Amazon Basics spinner is a plain, mid-size model with a spin knob and a non-skid base. It is a sensible choice for a household of one to three that eats salad most days.

Compared with the OXO 6.22 quart, it holds less and uses a simpler knob drive, and next to the Cuisinart, it is larger and has a removable colander basket. A knob can be tiring for a wet, heavy load, but it is also simple and rarely fails.

Rinse the lid and the basket after each use and let the parts dry before storing, since trapped moisture can sour. The plastic is lightweight, so avoid hot dishwasher racks that can warp it.
products.bestFor: A small household that wants a simple, mid-size spinner at a low cost.
pros: Mid-size bowl suits a household of one to three
Non-skid base keeps the spinner in place during use
Removable colander basket doubles as a washing bowl
Lower cost tier than the larger OXO models
cons: Knob drive is tiring when spinning a very large load
Plastic can warp in a very hot dishwasher cycle

products.name: OXO Good Grips glass salad spinner, borosilicate serving bowl, one-hand pump

specList.label: Use
specList.value: Serve and store in the bowl

products.description:
The glass OXO swaps the plastic bowl for a borosilicate glass one that can go to the table and into the fridge. A fitted lid lets you store the washed greens in the same bowl, which saves on dishes.

The pump and brake are the same one-hand design as the larger plastic OXO. Glass does not scratch, stain or hold smells like plastic, and it looks better on a table. The tradeoff is weight and fragility, and a higher cost tier. Compared with the stainless OXO, glass shows you the contents and handles the fridge well.

Care means taking the pump lid apart to rinse it, and handling the bowl with both hands near hard sink edges. Do not take the glass directly from a very hot rinse to a cold bowl, since sudden changes can stress it.
products.bestFor: A cook who wants to serve and store greens in the same glass bowl.
pros: Borosilicate glass bowl does not stain or hold odor like plastic
Bowl works for serving and for fridge storage with the lid
One-hand pump and brake keep drying quick and simple
Dishwasher safe parts make cleaning easy
cons: Glass is heavy and can break if dropped
Higher cost tier than the plastic models

products.name: OXO Good Grips stainless steel salad spinner, 6.34 qt
products.description:
The stainless OXO spinner keeps the pump and brake of the plastic model and swaps the bowl for stainless steel. A steel bowl does not crack, stain or pick up smells, and it keeps greens cool when chilled.

Its 6.34 quart capacity is the largest in this comparison, so it fits a whole head of lettuce plus herbs. Compared with the plastic OXO, it is more durable and more costly, and next to the glass version, it is lighter and tougher but does not let you see the contents.

Care is simple. Wash the bowl by hand or in the dishwasher, and rinse the lid mechanism. The steel does not show scratches, and the plastic lid and basket remain the wear parts. It is the longest-lasting design here.
products.bestFor: A heavy user who wants a durable bowl that will not crack or stain.
pros: Stainless steel bowl resists cracks, stains and odors for years
Largest capacity in the lineup suits big batches of greens
Chilled steel keeps leaves crisp while you prepare dinner
Pump and brake mechanism is easy to use with one hand
cons: Higher cost tier than the plastic models
Opaque bowl hides how much water has been removed

products.name: OXO Good Grips Little salad and herb spinner
products.description:
The Little spinner is the small version, made for herbs, baby greens, berries and a single serving of salad. It keeps the pump and brake design of the larger OXO but takes far less room.

It makes sense for someone who cooks with fresh herbs and needs them dry, or for a one-person household. Compared with the Amazon Basics 4.2 quart model, it holds much less but is easier to store. Next to the 6.22 quart OXO, it is not suited to a family salad.

Rinse the lid and basket after every use, as herb pieces collect in the mechanism. Plastic parts are the wear points, so replace the unit if the pump begins to slip.
products.bestFor: A single cook who washes herbs and small amounts of greens.
pros: Compact size fits a small cupboard and a small kitchen
Pump knob and brake match the larger models in ease of use
Gentle spin protects herbs and berries from bruising
Lower cost tier than the full-size spinners
cons: Capacity is too small for a family salad
Small basket needs several rounds for large heads of lettuce

products.name: Cuisinart salad spinner, 3 qt, wash, spin and dry greens
products.description:
The Cuisinart is a 3 quart spinner at the lowest cost tier in this group. It handles a modest bowl of salad for one or two people and is a good starter model.

A smaller bowl means more rounds for large amounts of lettuce, and the basic mechanism is less comfortable than a pump. Compared with the Amazon Basics 4.2 quart model, it holds less, and next to the OXO Little, it is larger but less refined. For a couple who eats a side salad now and then, it is enough.

Keep the lid clean and dry, and store it with the lid ajar so the parts air out. Replace the unit if the basket wobbles, since an unbalanced spin can rattle and splash. At this size, the other limit is leaf volume, so pack the basket loosely and never press the greens down, because compressed leaves trap water in the middle where the spin cannot reach.

pros: Lowest cost tier for a full-size bowl in this comparison
Three quart bowl suits a side salad for one or two

buyingCriteria.explanation: A pump knob like the OXO is quick and needs one hand, while a crank is steady but needs both hands, and a simple knob can tire your wrist. The pump spins faster with less effort, and a brake saves waiting for the basket to stop. A spinner that is hard to use ends up in a cupboard. A useful habit with any mechanism is to spin in short bursts, tip out the water that collects in the bottom of the bowl and then spin again, because water left in the bowl rises back into the leaves during a long single spin and defeats the purpose.

A 3 quart bowl suits a side salad, a 4 to 5 quart bowl suits two to three people, and a 6 quart bowl handles a family head of lettuce. Oversized bowls take cupboard space, so match the size to how much you wash at once. The 6.22 quart OXO and the 3 quart Cuisinart sit at the two ends.

Plastic is light and cheap but can scratch and hold smells, glass is clear and odor free but heavy, and stainless steel is the toughest and keeps greens cool. The glass OXO doubles as a serving bowl, and the stainless OXO resists dents and cracks.

A removable basket works as a colander for washing, and good drainage holes let water flow out. A deep basket holds more, while a shallow one needs more rounds. A basket that sits securely does not wobble during the spin.
A non-slip base keeps the bowl from walking across a counter, and a balanced basket avoids rattling. Cheap spinners shake, spray water and wobble. A wide, grippy base matters on a wet counter.

A spinner is bulky, so check the cupboard before buying. A bowl that nests or doubles as a storage dish saves space. Pump lids trap leaf bits and need a quick rinse, and glass and steel bowls are easiest to keep fresh.

howWeEvaluated.title: Spin comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared pump, knob and crank designs for effort and speed. The OXO pump models lead. This is based on the spec sheet and patterns in owner feedback.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched bowl size to household size, from the OXO Little to the 6.34 quart stainless. A bowl that is too large is as impractical as one that is too small.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bowl material
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared plastic, glass and stainless steel for durability and odor. The stainless and glass OXO lead for long term use. Plastic models ranked on cost.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at base design and basket balance. Non-slip bases earned credit. A spinner that walks across the counter ranks lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered dishwasher safety, lid design and nesting. The glass OXO doubles as a serving bowl. Bulky models were noted for storage. A spinner you cannot fit in a cupboard tends to live on the counter or never get used, so footprint counted as a real cost in our ranking.

maintenance.why: Leaf bits and dressing collect in the mechanism. A quick rinse stops smells and sticking.
Residue from greens and water spots build up. Dishwasher or warm soapy water both work.
Trapped moisture sours and grows film. Air the parts with the lid off.
A worn rubber ring slides and a worn brake lingers. Replace the unit if it becomes unsafe.

Cracks harbor bacteria and can shatter during a spin. Replace a cracked basket or lid. Hold the basket up to the light and look for hairline lines near the rim and around the center post, since those are the first places a basket fails under the stress of fast spinning.

faq.q: Do salad spinners really make a difference?
faq.a: Yes. Dry leaves hold dressing and stay crisp longer. A spinner removes much more water than patting with towels.

faq.q: How do I store washed lettuce?
faq.a: Spin it dry, then store it in a container lined with a paper towel in the fridge. Dry leaves keep much longer than wet ones. Tender greens such as butter lettuce and arugula bruise easily, so give them a gentler spin than sturdy romaine or kale, and wash them in cold water just before you plan to eat them.

faq.q: Is a pump better than a crank?
faq.a: A pump is quicker and one-handed, while a crank is steady and quiet. Choose by which feels better in your hand. If you have limited grip strength or joint pain, the pump with a brake is usually the easier choice, because it needs a simple downward press and no repeated wrist rotation.

faq.q: Can I use it for berries or herbs?
faq.a: Yes, at a gentle speed. A small spinner like the OXO Little protects delicate items from bruising.
Most are, but check the manual. Pump lids benefit from a hand rinse to clear trapped leaf bits.
An unbalanced load or a worn base is the usual cause. Spread the leaves evenly and replace a worn base ring.
